_comment: Battle of the Realm — the spoken cast.
The lines themselves are NOT here: tools/generate-voice.js reads them straight
out of scripts/battle/data.js, so editing the story never leaves the narration
quoting an old draft. Change a line there and re-run with --force for that id.
`voice` picks who says it. Put either an ElevenLabs voice ID or the exact name
of a voice in your account — run `node tools/generate-voice.js --list` to see
what you have. `description` is the character brief: paste it into ElevenLabs
Voice Design to build a bespoke voice, or let --design try to do it for you.
`settings` are ElevenLabs voice settings. Lower stability = more expressive and
more variable between takes; higher = steadier. The narrator wants steadiness,
Cast: George narrates. The villains are recast as monsters — Glob a whining,
shrieking boy-tyrant, Minyar a snivelling minion, Demonder a demon, Clubbo an
ogre. Short names work: the lookup matches the part before the " - ".
NOTE: every voice in the library is a normal human. Settings can make one
rant, rasp or lumber, but they cannot make it a monster. For genuinely
inhuman voices use Voice Design with the descriptions below:
which overwrites each `voice` field on success and leaves it alone on failure.

narrator.description: A warm, unhurried storyteller reading a children's picture book aloud at bedtime. Kind and a little wondrous, with a gentle smile behind the voice. Clear enough for a six-year-old to follow, never syrupy, never sinister. Mid-range, softly resonant, unhurried pacing with room to breathe between images.

glob.description: An evil boy-king with a voice that curdles — whining and wheedling one moment, shrieking with spite the next. Nasal, grating, self-pitying and cruel, a spoiled brat with real menace under the tantrum. Rises to a strangled screech when he does not get his way. Storybook villain: horrible, but funny-horrible, never truly frightening.
glob.casting_note: Charlie pushed to the edge: very low stability and very high style, so he rants and cracks instead of narrating.

minyar.description: A snivelling, grubby little minion — a nasal whining rasp, wheedling and resentful, the voice of a small nasty creature that bullies anything smaller and grovels to anything bigger. Grumbling, muttering, spiteful.
minyar.casting_note: Callum's husky trickster, wound up and soured into a whinging minion.

demonder.description: A demon — a deep, scorched, gravelly growl from somewhere far too large, with a rasp of smoke behind every word. Slow, certain and pitiless, amused by you the way a fire is amused by paper. Menacing but theatrical, a storybook demon rather than a horror one.
demonder.casting_note: Adam is the most dominant, firm voice in the roster — the closest a human library voice gets to a demon.

clubbo.description: An ogre — an enormous, rumbling, gravel-throated bellow, thick and slow and dim. Words come out in heavy blunt lumps with big gaps between them, like boulders dropped one at a time. Stupid, brutish and pleased with himself.
clubbo.casting_note: Brian is the deepest, most resonant voice available; high stability and near-zero style slow him into ogre-sized lumps.

casting._comment: which speaker reads each block of story text
